issues.explanation: For a life-threatening accident, 'Babies' as a salient auditory trigger is hard to connect clinically unless the accident specifically involved infants/crying, which is not supported by the rest of the profile. The other trigger items (intrusive thoughts, nightmare residue) are generic trauma reactivation cues, making this item stand out as trauma-incongruent.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Never Alone: make sure never to be alone with another person
issues.explanation: 'Make sure never to be alone with another person' suggests avoidance linked to fear of being accused of harming someone or of interpersonal/sexual threat, which is not coherently supported by the accident trauma type, threat items, or appraisals. The rest of the profile is organized around generalized danger/vulnerability, not being alone with another person specifically.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Humiliation: I feel permanently humiliated by what happened
issues.explanation: 'I feel permanently humiliated by what happened' is not impossible after an accident, but here it lacks support from the other selected items. The threat and strategy items focus on physical danger and hypervigilance, while no memory or trigger content suggests shame-based social exposure. In this profile, humiliation is the least coherent appraisal and appears disconnected from the accident-focused formulation.

vignette: Jin, a 33-year-old South Eastern Asian male and physical therapist, was involved in a life-threatening accident over six months ago that dramatically altered his daily experiences. Jin had been driving home from work when he lost control of his car on an icy patch, slamming into a tree at high speed. Since the accident, Jin has struggled with unwanted thoughts about the crash, often waking up from nightmares where he relives the moment of impact. The loud noises during those dreams and the subsequent intrusive thoughts have made him jumpy and easily startled in everyday life. Jin's body was severely injured in the accident, leaving him with a profound sense that his physical vulnerability has increased significantly. He now fears that any new pain or discomfort could be indicative of further damage he cannot trust his own body to reveal reliably. This fear is exacerbated by constant auditory triggers, such as loud noises from traffic or machinery at work, which often send Jin into a state of heightened alertness and concentration difficulties. These triggers have not only intensified Jin's sense of threat but also deepened his negative appraisals. He has come to believe that the world is unpredictable and dangerous, and you can never truly know who might harm you next. This belief has led him to adopt several maladaptive strategies as coping mechanisms. For instance, he compulsively cleans or organizes things repeatedly in an attempt to feel more in control of his environment. Jin also constantly scans his surroundings for potential weapons or signs of danger, mentally rehearsing worst-case scenarios to prepare himself. His negative appraisals have led him to adopt these maladaptive strategies as a means of dealing with the overwhelming sense of threat he experiences daily. For example, his compulsion to check and clean is driven by an intense need to mitigate the constant worry that another incident could happen at any moment. This cycle has further entrenched Jin's fear of harm, making it harder for him to trust even seemingly safe environments. At work as a physical therapist, Jin's heightened startle response and concentration difficulties have affected his ability to focus on patients' needs. He often finds himself checking the room for potential threats or cleaning supplies in between sessions, which has caused strain with colleagues who rely on his expertise and attention. His wife also notices that he becomes easily startled by loud noises at home, which sometimes leads to intense arguments as she tries to understand why such minor disturbances can trigger such strong reactions. Jin's sense of threat is exacerbated by these maladaptive strategies, as they serve to reinforce his negative appraisals about the world and his own vulnerability. For example, his constant scanning for potential weapons in any environment has made him more anxious and less able to relax or trust others, further entrenching his fear that harm can come from anywhere. What finally brought Jin to seek help was a particularly distressing incident at work where he had a panic attack while treating a patient. He realized then that these strategies were not just hindering his professional life but also straining his marriage and overall well-being. Jin is most afraid of never feeling safe again, but he hopes therapy will provide him with tools to manage his fears and regain trust in both himself and the world around him.
